#### **How will traffic disruptions be minimized during listed events and holidays?**

Construction work will not be performed on or near the highway carrying detoured STH 56 traffic during holiday weekends. The contractor will be required to have STH 56 open to traffic by 12:00 PM Friday for Memorial Day, Independence Day, and Labor Day.

#### **Describe how access to traffic generators (businesses, schools, etc.) and everyday services will be maintained:**

Local traffic, including emergency vehicles, school buses, postal delivery, and garbage collection will need to utilize alternate routes available near the closed segment of STH 56 to bypass the closed segment of STH 56. Through traffic will be directed to utilize the signed detour provided to bypass the closed segment of STH 56. No official access points exist within the closed segment of STH 56. Adjacent property owners, local officials and emergency services were notified of the project via mailing and they were asked to respond with any comments or concerns. At this time no comments or concerns have been received.

#### **Are there anticipated traffic impacts from the proposed project on other road/routes in the region/corridor?**

STH 56 traffic will be detoured to STH 82 and STH 131. It is not anticipated that the detoured STH 56 traffic will negatively impact the operations or roadway conditions of STH 82 or STH 131.

#### **Does the project affect other regions/states?**

No

| Memorial Day          | 05/27/2022 | 05/31/2022 |

| Labor Day             | 09/02/2022 | 09/06/2022 |

#### **How will traffic disruptions be minimized during listed events and holidays?**

The contract documents will contain standard special provisions that prohibit working on and hauling materials along or across any portion of STH 56, STH 82, or STH 131 during these holiday periods. Although the Labor Day Holiday falls outside of the anticipated end date, it has been included since the project is a working day contract and the exact construction dates are unknown and chosen by the contractor. The engineer will have the ability to suspend work activities beyond the periods listed above in the event any undesirable traffic congestion develops that has the potential to cause lengthy motorist delay or unsafe working conditions.

#### **Briefly describe the staging planned for maintaining traffic:** PROJECT 5130-00-80 WILL BE COMPLETED UTILIZING A SINGLE LANE, ONE-WAY TEMPORARY BYPASS STRUCTURE. TRAFFIC WILL BE CONTROLLED USING TEMPORARY TRAFFIC SIGNALS AT EACH END OF THE PROJECT. A TEMPORARY BYPASS WITH A TEMPORARY SIGNAL WAS DETERMINED TO BE THE MOST EFFECTIVE TRAFFIC MITIGATION STRATEGY DUE TO THE LENGTH AND DELAY OF AN ACCEPTABLE DETOUR ROUTE. IN ADDITION, THIS SEGMENT OF STH 71 ALSO SERVES STH 131 TRAFFIC BETWEEN ONTARIO AND TOMAH AND IS A CONDUIT FOR A LOCAL TRUCKING COMPANY TO IH 90 IN TOMAH. The project will be constructed under the following stages: Stage 1 will construct permanent sidewalk and curb ramps at the western project limits. Temporary pavement, temporary bypass structure and storm sewer crossings will be constructed during stage 1. Shoulder closures and flagging operations will be utilized during stage 1. Stage 2 will construct the permanent STH 71 structure and the left half of the roadway. Traffic will utilize single lane, one-way, bypass structure under temporary signals. Stage 3 will construct the eastbound STH 71 travel lane, lower pavement layer only. Eastbound traffic to utilize temporary bypass, westbound traffic to utilize permanent westbound lane/shoulder of STH 71 roadway. Stage 4 will remove the temporary bypass structure and complete riprap installation. Construct the right side curb & gutter, shoulder, sidewalk and guardrail under shoulder closure. The final eastbound travel lane surface will also be paved during this final stage. Stage 4 will feature uneven travel lanes until the completion of the final 2-Inch surface layer on the EB lane. #### **Describe how pedestrians will be accommodated during construction.** A permanent mid-block crossing with ADA ramps will be constructed during stage 1. This crossing will be utilized in the following construction stages along with a 5 foot wide sidewalk on the temporary bypass to accommodate pedestrians during construction. Stage 4 will utilize a temporary pedestrian crossing to maintain connectivity while the temporary bypass is being remove and the permanent south side sidewalk is constructed. #### **Vehicle Size Restrictions:** | # | Location Description | Min lane width to

Traffic models were analyzed using construction year (2020) traffic volumes for AM (7:15 AM to 8:15 AM) and PM (4:30 PM to 5:30 PM) peak hours. The eastbound approach (STH 105) is expected to operate at a LOS E during the PM peak period. Delay (35 seconds/vehicle) and queues (75-ft) are expected to remain minimal during this period. This movement currently operates at LOS E with similar delay and queue lengths. There is minor delay to STH 35 traffic due to turn lane closures. A Synchro traffic analysis was completed to represent flagging operations as closely as possible. It was determined from a 48-hour coverage count (site # 160310) on STH 35 that the largest nighttime hourly traffic volume is approximately 75% less than the PM peak hour traffic volumes. #### **How was the work zone capacity determined?**

STH 32 has a 2017 AADT of 13,000. The WisDOT planning-level forecasts do not show any traffic growth at this location, so for the purpose of this analysis a 2% annual growth rate was used. The construction year (2021) AADT would be approximately 14,000. This corridor has a Seasonal Factor Group (SFG) 2 for Urban Other. This results in a K30 value of 0.12 and a directional distribution of 59/41. The peak hour directional volume along STH 32 is estimated to be 990 vph. There is not expected to be any capacity issues along this portion of STH 32 since capacity of a single lane is expected to be higher than 1,000 vphpl. Capacity will be reduced even further at the STH 32 & STH 11 intersection due to closing one lane of the EB left turn movement and one NB thru lane. Synchro 11 and SimTraffic traffic modeling software, using Highway Capacity Manual (HCM) 6th Edition methodology, was used to estimate traffic conditions during these closures. Traffic Volumes were estimated based on AADTs on each leg of the intersection. - STH 11: 2017 AADT of 9,600 - STH 32 (South of STH 11): 2017 AADT 11,600 - STH 32 (North of STH 11): 2017 AADT 13,000 These AADTs were converted into K30 directional volumes based on a K30 value of 0.12 and an assume directional distribution of 50/50. Turning movement volumes were proportioned out based on the demand on each leg of the intersection and projected to year 2021 volumes using a 2% annual growth rate. It was determined that the intersection will remain under capacity. There will be minor delay due to these lane closures and queue lengths are not expected to be an issue. #### **Brief description of work activities:**

The existing structure (P-66-0709) is a single span precast prestressed box beam structure and is in poor condition. Deck delamination and spalling requires annual maintenance to maintain the deck in safe condition. Existing abutments are

spalling. Current Sufficiency Rating is 59.2 (February 13, 2019). The existing structure has no sidewalks therefore pedestrian traffic uses the roadway shoulders to cross the bridge. Structure replacement is required to provide safe travel for both vehicles and pedestrians. This project is located on North Wacker Drive approximately 0.2 miles north of the junction with STH 60 in the City of Hartford, Washington County, Wisconsin. The project includes the replacement of the existing Rubicon River bridge (P-66-0709) and its approaches on North Wacker Drive with a new structure B-66-199 which is proposed to be a single-span structure. Existing horizontal and vertical alignments will be maintained. ## **Section 2 - Project Description**

### **Brief description of work activities:**

Project ID 7650-00-04/74: The spot improvement project consists of replacing Culvert C-47-719 under STH 29 just south of 805th Avenue with a two-cell concrete box culvert B-47-0230. Due to the depth of the culvert, it is required to reconstruct the roadway for approximately 70' feet north and south of the culvert, install new guardrail along both sides of the roadway, and reconstruct the multi-use trail along the east side of the roadway. The existing safety rail along the multi-use trail will be salvaged and replaced. The reconstructed roadway will include a 7-inch asphaltic pavement over base aggregate and will maintain 12-foot travel lanes but will provide a wider 5-foot paved shoulder and 3-foot gravel shoulder. Centerline and shoulder rumble strips will be constructed. All new pavement marking will be installed as well. Project ID 7650-01-05/75: The pavement replacement project along STH 29 includes replacing the existing 7-inch concrete pavement with new 7-inch asphaltic pavement. The 12-foot travel lanes will be maintained, as well as the overall shoulder width of 8 feet; however, the paved shoulder will be widened to 5 feet. Both the roadway cross slope and the superelevation of the curve just south of the STH 29 and 690th Street intersection will be adjusted to current design standards. I-94 will remain open to traffic throughout construction with two-lanes in each direction during daytime hours (except to accommodate daytime cable barrier work - see TMP ID 7551) and a minimum of one-lane in each direction during overnight hours (as identified in Section 6). Interchange ramps to/from I-94 located within the project limits will remain open to traffic during daytime hours. Overnight ramp closures (3 to 4 total nights per location) are required to accommodate milling and paving operations on the ramps. Signed detours will be not be provided for the ramp closures. Current correspondence with impacted groups includes the minutes from the December 2018 Public Involvement Meeting, which are attached in this section.

### **Describe how impacts to transit users will be mitigated/coordinated:**

Several long distance intercity bus lines (Badger Bus, Greyhound, Megabus, Lamers) utilize this section of I-94. The roadway will remain open to traffic throughout the project. No impacts to the intercity long distance bus service are expected due to construction.

#### **Are there anticipated traffic impacts from the proposed project on other road/routes in the region/corridor?**

The majority of traffic is expected to continue using I-94 during construction (for analysis purposes, no diversion was assumed). The roadway will remain open to traffic throughout the project with two-lanes in each direction during daytime hours (except to accommodate daytime cable barrier work - see TMP ID 7551) and a minimum of one-lane in each direction during overnight hours (as identified in Section 6). Ramp closures are limited to overnight hours only, when traffic volumes are low. Therefore, no traffic impacts are anticipated on other roads/routes in the area.

### **Does the project affect other regions/states?**

The eastern project limits fall on the Jefferson/Waukesha County line, which is also the boarder between WisDOT Southwest Region (Jefferson County) and Southeast Region (Waukesha County). Mainline traffic control associated with the overnight lane closures will extend into the Southeast Region, but all construction activities will remain in the Southwest Region. Coordination with Southeast Region is ongoing and will continue throughout construction. The project does not affect another state.

### **List holidays or major special events that occur during the project:**

| Holiday/Special Event                    | Begin Date | End Date   |
|------------------------------------------|------------|------------|
| Memorial Day                             | 05/28/2021 | 06/01/2021 |
| Independence Day                         | 07/02/2021 | 07/06/2021 |
| Labor Day                                | 09/03/2021 | 09/07/2021 |
| Thanksgiving                             | 11/24/2021 | 11/29/2021 |
| Wisconsin Badger Home Football Game Days | 09/01/2021 | 12/11/2021 |
| Milwaukee Brewers Home Game Days         | 03/01/2021 | 11/15/2021 |

#### **How will traffic disruptions be minimized during listed events and holidays?**

No roadway work, lane closures, or hauling of materials will be allowed during the time periods listed above. Westbound lane closures are not permitted starting four hours prior to kickoff of a home game for the Wisconsin Badgers football team, concluding at kickoff. Eastbound lane closures are not permitted starting at half time of a home game for the Wisconsin Badgers football team, concluding six hours after completion of the game. Eastbound lane closures are not permitted starting three hours prior to start of a home game for the Milwaukee Brewers, concluding at the start of the game. Westbound lane closures are not permitted starting at the seventh inning of a home game for the Milwaukee Brewers, concluding three hours after the completion of the game.

--- End of Section 5 ---

#### **Describe how access to traffic generators (businesses, schools, etc.) and everyday services will be maintained:**

Access to traffic generators will be maintained throughout construction. The milling and paving operations along mainline STH 172 will be completed under traffic. Single lane closures will be permitted in both directions. A full closure will be required to complete the work along the single lane STH 172/IH 41 interchange ramps. Traffic will be detoured for the WB STH 172 ramp to SB IH 41 while the concrete pavement is being replaced. The detour will direct traffic along NB IH 41 to CTH VK (Lombardi Avenue). The work for the other single lane ramps will not have detours but lane closures will be allowed as specified in the lane closures.

#### **Describe how impacts to bicycle riders will be mitigated/coordinated:**

The curb ramps at the STH 172 & Packerland Drive/CTH EB and the STH 172 & Babcock Road intersections will be replaced with the project. While the curb ramps are being replaced the associated Packerland Drive bike trail will be closed and appropriate signage will be in place (see attached Traffic Control Plan). The public will be informed of the planned work and closure of the path through public involvement meetings, press releases/media alerts, the project website, and through the 511 Traveler Information Website.

#### **Describe how impacts to airports will be mitigated/coordinated:**

Airport personnel will be notified of the project and will be kept informed of changes in traffic control during construction by construction personnel. Lane closures will only be allowed during the times specified in the special provisions. The public will be informed of the planned work and lane closures through public involvement meetings, press releases/media alerts, the project website, and through the 511 Traveler Information Website.

#### **Are there anticipated traffic impacts from the proposed project on other road/routes in the region/corridor?**

IH 41 and CTH VK (Lombardi Avenue) traffic will be impacted by the project. Traffic along the WB STH 172 ramp to SB IH 41 will be detoured along NB IH 41 to CTH VK while the concrete pavement along the ramp is being replaced. The detour route will be signed per the traffic control plans.

No.

There will be integral curb and gutter, a 3-foot wide terrace, and 5-foot wide sidewalk on both sides of the roadway. The overall width of the roadway will be 76-feet for this section.
